lessons.title: What is PsA?
lessons.summary: PsA is a form of inflammatory arthritis linked to psoriasis.
lessons.body_markdown:
Psoriatic arthritis, or PsA, is listed in the provided RheumNotes materials as an autoimmune rheumatic disease that is strongly linked to psoriasis. Psoriasis is a condition that can cause inflamed, scaly skin.

The clinical-manifestations poster shows that PsA inflammation can affect joints, skin, nails, eyes, and the gut. Inflammation means swelling and irritation in body tissues. The poster also notes that inflammation may lead to lasting damage if it is left untreated.

PsA does not look the same in every person. The provided materials show several patterns, including joint inflammation, spine or sacroiliac-joint inflammation, tendon-attachment inflammation, whole-finger or whole-toe swelling, skin psoriasis, and nail changes. These patterns are organized more fully in later lessons.
key_takeaways: PsA is a form of inflammatory arthritis linked to psoriasis.
PsA can affect more than the joints.

lessons.title: PsA across the body
lessons.summary: PsA can appear in many body areas.
lessons.body_markdown:
The RheumNotes one-page PsA overview shows that inflammation can appear in many places. It highlights the spine and sacroiliac joints, shoulders, hips, elbows, wrists, hands, fingers, knees, ankles, and feet. It also shows skin or psoriasis, the eyes, and the gut.

The PsA and AS symptoms poster makes the same point visually. It marks the eyes, spine, shoulders, elbows, hips, gut, wrists, hands, fingers, skin, knees, ankles, and feet. The poster says that inflammation can strike throughout the body and can lead to long-term damage.

This broad pattern is important because PsA is not only a hand or knee problem. The source materials organize these different areas into disease domains so that the full pattern can be considered together.
key_takeaways: PsA can appear in many body areas.
Joint, skin, nail, eye, and gut findings may all be part of the picture.

lessons.title: The CASPAR starting point
lessons.summary: CASPAR starts with inflammatory articular disease.
lessons.body_markdown:
The provided PsA one-pager shows the CASPAR criteria, a set of classification criteria for psoriatic arthritis. CASPAR stands for Classification Criteria for Psoriatic Arthritis.

Before points are counted, the source shows an entry requirement: established inflammatory articular disease. In the one-pager, this can involve a joint, the spine, or an enthesis. An enthesis is the place where a tendon or ligament attaches to bone.

The handwritten PsA mind map repeats this structure: first establish inflammatory articular disease involving a joint, spine, or enthesis, and then consider the CASPAR point features. The point features are covered in the next lesson.
key_takeaways: CASPAR starts with inflammatory articular disease.
The starting disease can involve joints, spine, or entheses.

lessons.title: What counts in CASPAR
lessons.summary: CASPAR uses several features rather than one single finding.
lessons.body_markdown:
After the CASPAR entry requirement is met, the one-pager says a total of at least 3 points is used in the criteria. The source lists several features.

- Current skin or scalp psoriasis counts for 2 points. A personal history or family history can count for 1 point in the situations shown in the table.
- Nail dystrophy counts for 1 point. Nail dystrophy means changes such as pitting, separation of the nail from the nail bed, or thickening under the nail.
- A negative rheumatoid factor, or RF, counts for 1 point.
- Current or previously documented dactylitis counts for 1 point. Dactylitis is swelling of an entire finger or toe.
- The source also lists new bone formation next to a joint on an X-ray as a 1-point feature.

The criteria combine these findings rather than relying on only one feature.
key_takeaways: CASPAR uses several features rather than one single finding.
Current psoriasis carries more points than personal or family history in the source table.

lessons.title: Six core PsA domains
lessons.summary: The source organizes PsA into six core GRAPPA domains.
lessons.body_markdown:
The GRAPPA poster groups PsA into six core treatment domains. A domain is a major pattern of disease that can be active on its own or with other patterns.

- Peripheral arthritis: inflammatory synovitis of joints in the arms or legs. Synovitis means inflammation of a joint lining.
- Axial disease: inflammation of the spine and sacroiliac joints, which can cause inflammatory back pain and stiffness.
- Enthesitis: inflammation where tendons or ligaments attach to bone, commonly at the Achilles tendon or plantar fascia.
- Dactylitis: swelling of a whole finger or toe from joint, tendon-sheath, and soft-tissue inflammation.
- Skin psoriasis: well-defined red plaques with silvery scale.
- Nail psoriasis: changes such as pitting, onycholysis, oil-drop change, or thickening under the nail. Onycholysis means the nail separates from the nail bed.
key_takeaways: The source organizes PsA into six core GRAPPA domains.
Each domain describes a different way PsA can appear.

lessons.title: Other areas PsA can affect
lessons.summary: PsA symptoms can extend beyond the most obvious joints.
lessons.body_markdown:
The clinical-manifestations poster shows PsA findings in many body areas.

For the eyes, it lists anterior uveitis, an inflammation in the front of the eye, with redness, pain, and sensitivity to light. For the gut, it describes inflammation similar to inflammatory bowel disease, or IBD, with pain, bloating, or changes in bowel habits.

The poster also shows inflammation around the shoulders, elbows, hips, knees, and ankles. Wrists, hands, and fingers can have joint swelling, dactylitis, and nail changes. Feet can have enthesitis, especially near the Achilles tendon and plantar fascia. The spine and sacroiliac joints can be painful and stiff when inflamed.

A second source poster uses a body map to show many of these same areas.
key_takeaways: PsA symptoms can extend beyond the most obvious joints.
The source posters include eye and gut manifestations as well as many joint areas.

lessons.title: Common PsA comorbidities
lessons.summary: A comorbidity is another health condition that occurs with PsA.
lessons.body_markdown:
A comorbidity is another health condition that is present along with PsA. The provided RheumNotes poster lists ten common comorbidities and gives percentages from the source used to make that poster.

The poster lists hypertension at 34%, metabolic syndrome at 29%, obesity at 27%, hyperlipidemia at 24%, and cardiovascular disease at 19%. It also lists type 2 diabetes at 13%, pulmonary disease at 12%, depression at 12%, thyroid disease at 11%, and gastrointestinal disease at 10%.

The poster describes hypertension as high blood pressure and hyperlipidemia as elevated cholesterol or triglycerides. Metabolic syndrome is described as central obesity together with hypertension, abnormal blood fats, and insulin resistance. These percentages belong to the provided poster and may depend on how comorbidities were defined in its source studies.
key_takeaways: A comorbidity is another health condition that occurs with PsA.
The source poster lists cardiovascular, metabolic, mood, lung, thyroid, and gastrointestinal conditions.

lessons.title: Why domains guide treatment
lessons.summary: Different active PsA domains can change treatment choices.
lessons.body_markdown:
The PsA one-pager says to assess every GRAPPA domain and choose therapy that covers as many active domains as possible. The reason is that different PsA patterns do not always respond to the same treatment class.

For peripheral arthritis, the source emphasizes treating the joints to a target. A DMARD is a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug. For axial disease, it notes that conventional synthetic DMARDs, or csDMARDs, do not treat the spine and lists other treatment classes used for axial disease. For enthesitis and dactylitis, the source says these findings can influence selection of biologic or targeted synthetic DMARD classes.

Skin and nail psoriasis can also steer treatment choice. The one-pager links these domains with cytokine-targeting classes such as IL-17, IL-23, and TNF inhibitors. IL means interleukin, and TNF means tumor necrosis factor. Both are cytokines, which are signaling proteins used by immune cells.

This lesson describes the organization shown in the source and does not rank medicines or recommend an individual treatment.
key_takeaways: Different active PsA domains can change treatment choices.
The source says to assess every domain rather than looking at only one symptom.

lessons.title: Main treatment class ideas
lessons.summary: The source describes conventional, biologic, and targeted synthetic DMARD categories.
lessons.body_markdown:
The management chapter describes several broad treatment categories used across inflammatory arthritis and autoimmune disease.

Conventional synthetic DMARDs, or csDMARDs, are disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs made as traditional small-molecule medicines. The chapter describes them as an early form of disease-modifying treatment.

Biologic therapies are engineered proteins designed to block specific signaling molecules or cell targets. The source explains that the biologic era expanded from TNF to other pathways and specifically notes the IL-17 and IL-23 pathway in psoriatic arthritis.

Targeted synthetic DMARDs, or tsDMARDs, are small-molecule medicines aimed at specific signaling systems. JAK means Janus kinase, and TYK2 means tyrosine kinase 2. The chapter describes JAK inhibitors as working at signaling points inside cells and TYK2-selective therapy as acting on pathways relevant to psoriasis and PsA.

These are treatment classes, not instructions about which medicine a person should use.
key_takeaways: The source describes conventional, biologic, and targeted synthetic DMARD categories.
Biologics act on specific outside-cell targets; JAK and TYK2 medicines act on signaling inside cells.

lessons.title: Tracking disease activity
lessons.summary: The source uses minimal disease activity as one way to summarize PsA activity.
lessons.body_markdown:
The provided PsA mind map includes minimal disease activity, or MDA, as a treatment target. MDA is a combined way of looking at several parts of disease activity rather than relying on one symptom.

The mind map notes seven areas used in the MDA framework: tender-joint count, swollen-joint count, enthesitis count, skin activity, patient pain, the patient's global rating of disease activity, and physical function. It notes meeting 5 of the 7 criteria.

The preface to Murphy's Laws of Arthritis also names MDA as a validated composite index for psoriatic arthritis. A composite index is a score or target that combines several kinds of information.

This framework helps explain why PsA follow-up can include joints, skin, tendon-attachment pain, function, and the patient's own experience at the same time.
key_takeaways: The source uses minimal disease activity as one way to summarize PsA activity.
Disease activity can be tracked with several measures rather than a single symptom.

lessons.title: The four pillars framework
lessons.summary: The source presents nutrition, movement, mind, and sleep as four connected pillars.
lessons.body_markdown:
The Four Pillars of Arthritis organizes daily-life factors into four connected areas: nourishment, movement, mastery of the mind, and sleep.

The chapter describes nourishment as the food and nutrients that support the body. Movement is presented as maintenance for strength and function. The mind is described as a command center that affects attention, stress, and how a person responds to symptoms. Sleep is presented as a major period of restoration.

The source treats these areas as parts of one system rather than isolated habits. It says the pillars reinforce one another. For example, pain or poor sleep may make movement harder, while movement, nutrition, and mental practices can influence how a person experiences daily life with arthritis.

This is a general arthritis framework from the approved materials. It is educational and does not replace PsA medical treatment.
key_takeaways: The source presents nutrition, movement, mind, and sleep as four connected pillars.
The four-pillar framework is general arthritis education, not a replacement for medical treatment.

lessons.title: Movement and the mind
lessons.summary: The source describes movement as the second pillar.
lessons.body_markdown:
The Four Pillars chapter calls movement the second pillar. It discusses resistance or isotonic exercise, Tai Chi, yoga, Pilates, cycling, and water-based movement as examples studied in arthritis. Isotonic exercise means a muscle changes length while working against resistance.

The chapter presents movement as a way to support strength, function, balance, and confidence. Its examples come from different arthritis populations, so they are not presented here as a PsA-specific exercise prescription.

The third pillar is called mastery and focuses on the mind. The chapter discusses mindfulness, meditation, prayer, and other reflective practices in relation to pain, stress, attention, and coping. It describes the mind as influencing how a flare is interpreted and how a person continues other health-supporting routines.

These are educational concepts from the source, not individualized instructions.
key_takeaways: The source describes movement as the second pillar.
The third pillar focuses on the mind and coping with chronic symptoms.

lessons.title: Nourishment and sleep
lessons.summary: Nourishment and sleep are two of the four source pillars.
lessons.body_markdown:
Nourishment is the first pillar in The Four Pillars of Arthritis. The chapter discusses whole foods, protein, fats, complex carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and plant compounds as parts of the body's nutritional environment. It also stresses that single supplements are not disease-modifying drugs.

Sleep is the fourth pillar. The source describes sleep as a period when the body restores tissues, regulates the nervous system, and resets parts of immune and inflammatory activity. It connects disrupted sleep with worse pain, fatigue, and reduced ability to use the other pillars.

Near the end of the chapter, the four pillars are brought together: nutrition supplies materials and signals, movement supports structure and function, the mind shapes attention and coping, and sleep helps consolidate recovery.

This summary keeps the source's framework without giving a diet, supplement dose, or sleep prescription.
key_takeaways: Nourishment and sleep are two of the four source pillars.
The source connects sleep with restoration and nourishment with the materials the body uses.

lessons.title: Symptoms to report
lessons.summary: The source poster says to talk with a healthcare provider about symptoms in the highlighted areas.
lessons.body_markdown:
The provided PsA and ankylosing spondylitis symptoms poster gives a direct patient message: talk to your healthcare provider if you notice symptoms in the areas shown.

Those areas include the eyes, spine, shoulders, elbows, hips, gut, wrists, hands and fingers, skin or psoriasis, knees, ankles, and feet. The clinical-manifestations poster adds examples such as joint pain or swelling, stiffness in the spine or sacroiliac joints, a whole swollen finger or toe, tendon-attachment pain, nail changes, and inflamed skin plaques.

The purpose of this topic is to help a patient recognize which kinds of changes the provided materials connect with PsA and bring them to the care team's attention. The source materials do not provide a detailed emergency-triage list, so this lesson does not add one.
key_takeaways: The source poster says to talk with a healthcare provider about symptoms in the highlighted areas.
PsA-related symptoms may occur in joints, skin, eyes, gut, spine, and feet.

lessons.title: Eye and gut changes
lessons.summary: The source includes eye inflammation and gut inflammation among PsA-related manifestations.
lessons.body_markdown:
Two of the source materials call attention to symptoms outside the joints.

For the eyes, the clinical-manifestations poster lists anterior uveitis. Uveitis means inflammation inside the eye. The poster describes redness, pain, and sensitivity to light. The PsA one-pager also lists uveitis as a related condition and says to coordinate with ophthalmology, the medical specialty for eye care.

For the gut, the clinical-manifestations poster describes inflammation similar to inflammatory bowel disease, or IBD. It lists pain, bloating, or changes in bowel habits. The PsA one-pager also lists IBD, including Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis, as a related condition that can influence treatment choices.

These descriptions explain why the care team may ask about eye and gut symptoms as part of the full PsA picture.
key_takeaways: The source includes eye inflammation and gut inflammation among PsA-related manifestations.
The one-pager specifically says uveitis should be coordinated with ophthalmology.
